subject: Readiness check: QBR renewal thermometer & exec triggers
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara_nguyen@crescentanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@crescentanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: June QBR — renewal prep & ask list

Karthik / Jordan —

Thanks for running point on the QBR. As we discussed in last week’s sync, Crescent’s renewal window opens mid-July. Before the exec readout we need: a renewal heatmap, outstanding procurement blockers, and any exec-level asks (credits/SLAs/feature commitments).

Quick context: adoption has been steady but token spend is up 32% this quarter driven by R&D experimentation. Procurement is flagging the current contract terms on data residency and retention. Tom and I would like a summary we can share with our CFO and procurement team by June 18.

Can you confirm:
- a single-page heatmap (risk: high/medium/low) for the renewal decision makers
- list of outstanding redlines we can accelerate (I attached the current redlines PDF)
- any recommended executive asks for making the renewal a go/no-go

Attachments: Crescent_contract_redlines_v3.pdf (redlines from legal)

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of Machine Learning, Crescent Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: June QBR — renewal prep & ask list

Forwarding Crescent's note — they need a crisp package by 6/18 for their execs. Jordan, can you own the heatmap + procurement blockers? Lauren, can you surface any OKR tie-ins (adoption, cost/unit, SLOs) so we can frame asks vs. outcomes? Grace, FYI — may need an exec approval for a one-off credit or SLA tweak.

Proposed deliverables and owners:
- Renewal heatmap (Jordan) — single slide, scorecard, 3x risk drivers
- Redline acceleration plan (Jordan + Legal) — identify 2 negotiable items, 1 hard no
- OKR alignment memo (Lauren) — 1-pager linking renewal to product OKRs and cost optimization roadmap
- Exec ask summary (Karthik) — suggested credit levels, SLA revisions, and fallback model routing options

Timeline:
- Drafts due 6/16 EOD
- Internal review 6/17 morning (leadership stakeholders)
- Final package out to Crescent 6/18 noon

I also attached the redlines Sara sent — FYI.

Karthik
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara_nguyen@crescentanalytics.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@crescentanalytics.com>, procurement@crescentanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: June QBR — renewal prep & ask list

Team —

Initial heatmap draft attached (renewal-heatmap-crescent.xlsx). High-level callouts:
1) Commercial risk (HIGH) — spend volatility + unaligned spend caps. They’re testing multiple LLM routes; unit economics unknown.
2) Technical risk (MEDIUM) — data residency redline and audit log retention are active blockers; engineering can offer a committable roadmap but not immediate change.
3) Product fit (LOW) — features roadmap matches top use cases; adoption in prod is limited to 2 pilots.

Top 3 executive asks I recommend:
- 6% one-time renewal credit tied to committed monthly spend (cuts through their CFO friction)
- SLA addendum: 99.5% availability for production routes used in payments/CRM (limited to 1-year term)
- Commitment proposal: 9-month pilot to full enterprise migration with quarterly checkpoints (gives them runway to validate ROI)

Procurement redlines: they want explicit data retention < 90 days and a right-to-audit clause removed. Legal suggests we offer a compromise: standard retention with an option for isolated logs retention for audit requests (costed).

I’ll incorporate Lauren’s OKR framing once I have the bullet points — Jordan

Attachments: renewal-heatmap-crescent.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara_nguyen@crescentanalytics.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@crescentanalytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: June QBR — renewal prep & ask list

Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the clear ask. We’ll deliver a single-slide heatmap, a short redline escalation plan, and a 1-page OKR alignment memo by the 6/18 deadline. Early signals: Jordan recommends a targeted one-time 6% credit tied to committed spend and a time-limited SLA addendum for critical routes. Legal is preparing a compromise on retention/audit language that avoids a permanent right-to-audit clause.

Executive ask for your side: please confirm the CFO’s tolerance for a one-time credit vs. a multi-year price rework. If the CFO prefers runway, we can instead propose a phased commitment with quarterly cost reviews.

Next steps (internal): Jordan to finalize heatmap + procurement summary by EOD 6/16; Lauren to drop OKR bullets by 6/16 morning; Karthik to draft exec ask summary for internal review 6/17 AM.

I’ll circulate the final package to your team on 6/18 noon PT. If you want an early readout for procurement before that, let me know and we’ll prioritize a short call.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachments: qbr-okr-alignment-notes.md (internal notes)
